819:
Liberty County has established solid waste management services and facilities for authorized use by the residents, municipalities, and commercial and business establishments located in the jurisdictional boundaries of the county. This article details the authorized use of these specific facilities, sets forth user fees for specific facilities and establishes penalties for unauthorized use of said facilities.
(Code 1987, § 15-201; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006)
820:
(a) Transfer station. This facility accepts conforming nonhazardous solid waste from collection sources such as jurisdictional municipal solid waste collection services (public and privately owned), county-operated solid waste collection services (rural and commercial clients), jurisdictional commercial and business (contract and cash) customers and nonjurisdictional private residential and nonjurisdictional commercial and business clients. All solid waste processed into the transfer station is charged a published disposal fee based on the customer and the solid waste material. Disposal fees are established by the county board of commissioners (see section 34-71) and are periodically adjusted. The current fee schedule is available through the county solid waste, at the transfer station.
(b) Convenience centers. These facilities, located throughout the unincorporated area of the county, provide interim solid waste disposal/collection points for the unincorporated residents and municipal residents of Allenhurst, Flemington, Gumbranch, Midway, Riceboro and Walthourville. (This excludes Hinesville residents who have full range solid waste collection provided by the city and thus are not assessed for associated operational/disposal costs.) These convenience centers are for use by single-family residential property owners of the unincorporated area and municipalities described above. Operational costs for these facilities are recouped through the county solid waste assessment. Use by unauthorized commercial and business or nonjurisdictional parties is prohibited. Typically, each center includes one household waste compactor with a 38- to 40-cubic-yard enclosed receiving container and two 40-cubic-yard open top containers for disposal of yard waste, scrap metal and appliances (white goods) and bulky waste (brown goods). Additionally, each center provides facilities for acceptance of recyclable items. Service fees (annual residential solid waste assessment) for authorized customers are established by the county board of commissioners (see section 34-71) and are periodically adjusted. A listing of these fees is available, through the county solid waste authority, at the commissioner's office or at the county solid waste authority transfer station.
(c) Rural dumpster sites. The county operates several rural dumpster sites in the unincorporated area of the county. Until these sites are closed, their use is restricted to those jurisdictional residents who pay for their operation through the annual residential solid waste assessment. Use by non-jurisdictional parties and/or commercial or business enterprises is strictly prohibited.
(d) Recycling facilities. Six additional recycling facilities are located in the municipal boundaries of Hinesville (four locations), Walthourville (one facility) and Riceboro (one facility). These facilities, in addition to those co-located at each convenience center, are operated by the county solid waste for the sole use of county residents. No business or commercial use is authorized. The disposal of any type of nonconforming waste is unauthorized at these facilities. Recyclable items are to be placed in the appropriate bins or containers. Operational costs of these facilities are recouped through the annual residential solid waste assessment.
(Code 1987, § 15-202; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)
821:
User fees have been established by the county board of commissioners for each of the facilities described above and are detailed in article II of this chapter. These fees are periodically adjusted by the board of commissioners. Current approved fee schedules are available at the commissioner's office or at the county solid waste transfer station.
(Code 1987, § 15-202.1; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)
822:
(a) Generally. The cost to operate the county convenience centers, rural dumpster sites and recycling facilities is funded by the annual residential solid waste assessment. Use of these facilities is strictly reserved for residents of the county who pay for their operation through the annual assessment. Unauthorized users will be cited and include those who plan to use (are physically located at a site) or have used a facility to discard solid waste or recyclables and persons who are scavenging or have scavenged items from the solid waste collection containers or recycling facilities. Unauthorized users will be cited and will be subject to court fees, fines and disposal costs as determined by the county magistrate court, the table of offenses, fines and disposal charges (see section 34-105) and the county solid waste.
(b) Proof of authorization. The prima facie evidence of unauthorized use is the user's vehicle license plate. Out-of-county plates suggest the user is unauthorized. However, the out-of-county user is authorized to use the facility if they have received and paid the current annual residential solid waste assessment. A current paid receipt for the solid waste assessment supported by a second form of personal identification validates the authorized facility use by such residents. Officers of the county charged with validating solid waste facility users are to explain the reasons for verifying the user's residency; advise the out-of-county user to carry a copy of the paid solid waste assessment receipt; take the users name, home address and telephone number and license plate number and allow use of the facility. The name, address, license plate number and phone number will be transmitted to the litter control deputy for validation of authorized use. Fraudulent cases will be cited for unauthorized use through magistrate court.
(c) Identification. Unauthorized users will be identified as follows:
(1) Observation by the county litter control deputy or other solid waste employee. Observed use includes the physical act of waste disposal or being at a site with the intent to use the facility for waste disposal; or being on site to scavenge; being found in the act of scavenging; or found with scavenged material in their possession.
(2) Reporting of apparent unauthorized use by the general public under the silent witness program or by calling the offices of the county commission or the solid waste authority. In such cases, prima facie evidence is being on site using a vehicle with an out-of-county license plate or operation of a vehicle with affixed business logo operated by the potential offender who has or plans to dispose of waste typical of the business, and, if available, a description of the individual and the vehicle, the time and facility being used, and the type of waste being disposed of or scavenged. Additional evidence of unauthorized use is identifiable discards of solid waste (letters, bank receipts, credit card slips, magazines with address labels, shipping containers with ship-to addresses, business papers, etc.). Reports of this type will be accepted telephonically, in writing or verbally.
(3) Apprehension by an officer of the law. In this case, the apprehending officer will issue a citation to the offending party. No warnings will be given.
(4) After-the-fact clean-up of materials disposed of at any of the county facilities or materials discarded elsewhere in the county (private or publicly owned lands). In such cases, prima facie evidence will be any item recovered from the discards which bears a name, address or other form of personal identification which would indicate the last ownership of the improperly discarded items.
(d) Citation. Citations for unauthorized use of a county solid waste collection/disposal/recycling facility, unless issued by an officer of the law other than the county litter control deputy, will be written by the county litter control deputy and prosecuted through the county magistrate court. No warning will be issued since all facilities have been signed advising that unauthorized use is prohibited.
(e) Payment of fines and disposal charges. The county magistrate court will prosecute each case. The county solid waste authority will provide the court with calculated weight tickets detailing the associated pull fees, disposal charges and clean-up costs as appropriate for each citation. These costs are to be added to the fines presented in the tables of offenses, fines and disposal charges shown below. Upon payment to the court, the applicable fines and disposal charges will to turned over to the county solid waste through the office of the Clerk of the Superior Court.
(Code 1987, § 15-203; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)

827:
There is hereby established a uniform system for the naming of all roads, streets and public ways in the unincorporated areas of the county.
(Code 1987, § 15.5-1; Ord. No. 2010-009, § I, 9-7-2010)
Cross reference— Address numbering and street names, 8-380 et seq.
828:
(a) The board of commissioners shall establish and assign names for all streets, roads and public ways in the unincorporated areas of the county.
(b) Unless otherwise determined appropriate by the board of commissioners, no new road name assigned by the board of commissioners shall be a duplicate of or be similar to (either phonetically or by spelling) any existing street name in the unincorporated areas of the county.
(c) Existing duplicate or similar road names shall be changed only as necessary to ensure the effectiveness and efficiency of the enhanced 911 system in the county, as determined in the judgment of the board of commissioners.
(d) Historical names shall be the prime consideration in the assignment of road names, but shall not be the only or determinative consideration.
(e) Unless otherwise determined appropriate by the board of commissioners, as many segmental roads as practical shall be identified as being a continuous road so as to reduce unnecessary road identifying names and numbers.
(f) The county paved roads and historical roads, whether paved or unpaved, shall be named, and as funds are available the names and county road numbers shall be posted. Road naming within subdivisions shall comply with the county subdivision regulations and in addition be approved by the county 911 division prior to the final subdivision plat being approved and recorded in the office of the clerk of superior court of the county.
(g) In the event there is a dispute as to the proper name of an existing road or a dispute as to whether an existing road has been previously officially named, the board of commissioners, in its absolute discretion, shall assign a name to the road under the same procedure for the naming of a new road. The decision by the board of commissioners as to the name assigned to such road shall be final and conclusive.
(Code 1987, § 15.5-2; Ord. No. 2010-009, § I, 9-7-2010)
Cross reference— Address numbering and street names, 8-380 et seq.
829:
(a) Upon receipt of a petition in the form and format as specified by the board of commissioners seeking a change of name of an existing named road, the board of commissioners shall take under consideration, but be under no compulsion to grant, said request; provided that any such petition shall contain the signatures of the owners or their authorized representatives (as specified below) of not less than 60 percent of the parcels of property abutting said public road. At its discretion, the board of commissioners may, but shall not be required, to hold a public hearing prior to deciding the issue of the proposed name change.
(b) For purposes of this section, the owner of the abutting property shall be deemed to be the person or entity returning the property for ad valorem taxes in the office of the county tax commissioner.
(1) If the property is returned in the name of an estate or trust, the legal representative of the estate or trust must sign the petition.
(2) If the property is returned in the name of a corporation or a limited liability company, an authorized corporate officer, member, or manager, as the case may be, must sign the petition on behalf of said legal entity.
(3) If the property is returned in the name of a partnership, each partner must sign the petition unless the signing partner has written authorization to sign for all other partners.
(4) The determination by the board of commissioners as to the authority of the person signing the petition and the number of parcels abutting the road shall be final and conclusive.
(c) Absent exigent circumstances (as determined by the board of commissioners in its absolute discretion), no petition to change the name of an existing public roadway will be considered if:
(1) The name of said roadway has been changed within the previous 120 months; or
(2) If a petition to change the name of said roadway has been denied by the board of commissioners within the previous 120 months.
(Code 1987, § 15.5-3; Ord. No. 2010-009, § I, 9-7-2010)
Cross reference— Address numbering and street names, 8-380 et seq.

837:
This article is intended to require notice of timber harvesting operations within the unincorporated areas of Liberty County pursuant to O.C.G.A. §12-6-24, and, in accordance with Title 32 of the Official Code of Georgia, provide regulations further governing use of public roads by persons engaged in said timber harvesting operations in order to assure the public safety and to protect the county roadways and environment.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
838:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
County administrator means the county administrator for Liberty County, or his or her designee.
Notice means the notice required to be given to the public works department by the timber harvester as provided herein.
Person means any natural person, firm, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or other legal entity of whatever form.
Public works department means the Liberty County Public Works Department.
Public works director means the Director of the Liberty County Public Works Department.
Surety bond means a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in the State of Georgia, protecting the County against any damage caused by such person or firm in an amount specified by the governing authority of Liberty County not exceeding $5,000.00 or, at the option of the timber harvester, a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of an in lieu of such bond. Any such surety bond or letter of credit shall be in form prescribed by or acceptable to the county administrator and shall be for the calendar year in which delivered; provided that no more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each timber harvester, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
Timber means softwood or hardwood trees harvested for commercial purposes.
Timber harvester means any person harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Liberty County, Georgia for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
839:
(a) Written notice shall be required of any timber harvester harvesting timber in the unincorporated areas of the County for each separate tract to be harvested. Said written notice shall be (a) delivered to the public works department prior to entering onto the subject tract, if possible, but in no event later than 24 hours after entering onto said tract; and (b) in such form and containing such information as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24(b)(1). Notice shall be effective only as to the tract described therein upon receipt by the public works department (as confirmed by written acknowledgment from said public works department to the timber harvester) and compliance with all other applicable requirements of this article. Further, within 24 hours following completion of timber harvesting operations, the responsible timber harvester shall give notice of cessation of cutting to the public works director or other designee of the county administrator. Such notice may be given in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile, e-mail, or such other means as approved by the governing authority of the county, or by mail.
(b) Upon notification published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required by this article may do so at their option, and the county will accept notifications submitted in this manner. On and after a date specified and published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, use of the aforesaid state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this article. On and after said date, submission of the notice by any of the means listed in this section shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this article.
(c) At all times during any timber harvesting operations subject to this article, the timber harvester shall additionally ensure that the requisite notice is continuously posted and displayed in good condition and in a conspicuous location on each tract of land identified in said notice. For purposes of this section, the notice shall be deemed posted in a "conspicuous location" if clearly visible and located in the immediate vicinity where the entrance road or trail providing vehicular access to the subject tract meets the nearest public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
840:
(a) A surety bond shall not be required prior to notice becoming effective. However, following the giving of any notice, in the event that the public works director determines that any activities relating to the timber harvesting are being conducted in a manner that poses likelihood of damage to any public rights-of-way or danger to the public safety, the public works department shall be authorized to demand a surety bond from the timber harvester. The surety bond shall be delivered to the public works department within three business days following receipt of written demand for the same, unless within said time a written notice of appeal is received by the public works department contesting the requirement of the surety bond. In the event of such contest, the public works department shall, no later than five business days, schedule an administrative hearing in such matter before the county administrator, who shall deliver a decision within three business days of said hearing. The decision of the county administrator shall be conclusive and binding for all purposes. Following any contest as provided above, all timber harvesting authorized pursuant to the applicable notice shall be suspended until the surety bond, if any, is delivered to the public works department as required by the county administrator.
(b) The bond or letter of credit required by this section shall protect the county against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including tree tops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damages or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within 500 feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation.
(c) In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this article is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered by the timber harvester to the public works department within five business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the timber harvester caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to $7,500.00 after the first revocation, and $10,000.00 after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed $10,000.00.
(d) In no event shall the delivery of a surety bond (or the failure to require a surety bond) limit the liability of any person engaged in timber harvesting and related activities for damages to public property or rights-of-way or for other personal injury or property damage, and all such persons shall be and remain at all times fully liable to the county for any and all such injury and damage. Furthermore, the right of the county to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of this article shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
841:
(a) When damage results from a timber harvester's activities, the public works director or such other designee of the county administrator shall make and provide a written claim to the timber harvester causing the damage within 30 business days after the public works director becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with subsection (b) immediately below, give the timber harvester the opportunity to repair such damage within 30 days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the public works director or other designee of the county administrator determines that the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the timber harvester and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the timber harvester and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided in this section the public works director or other designee of the county administrator shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this article.
(b) Within 30 days of receipt of the written claim described in subsection (a) immediately above, the timber harvester against whom the claim is submitted may:
(1) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator, the public works director or other designee of the county administrator shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five business days to the timber harvester and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(2) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a 30 day extension to repair the damage from the public works director or other designee of the county administrator who provided written notice of the claim, provided that no extensions shall exceed 90 days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator.
(3) Appeal the claim to the Magistrate Court of Liberty County. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The magistrate court will hear evidence and arguments within 30 days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the 30-day period, or any extension thereof, required by subsection (b)(2) above. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the timber harvester against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit, and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the county, the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment accordingly; the county shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court, up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(c) In the event the timber harvester against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under subsection (b) above within the time required therein, said timber harvester shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
842:
Prior to commencing timber harvesting operations, the public works director shall inspect the point of access to the public road from the tract described in the notice in order to determine its suitability. If a culvert is required at the point of access, it shall be promptly installed by the timber harvester as directed by the public works director. (Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
843:
Prior to commencing any timber harvesting operations, the timber harvester shall post two signs in each direction from the point of access onto the involved public road. One sign at a distance of 1,000 feet from the point of access stating "Warning: Logging Operations Ahead," and one sign at a distance of 500 feet stating "Slow Truck Entering Highway." All signs shall be 36 inches × 36 inches, erected in a diamond shape, painted orange with black legend and posted at least three feet from the travel surface of the roadway. Prior to and at all times during any timber harvesting operations subject to this article, the timber harvester shall additionally ensure that the requisite notice is continuously posted and displayed in good condition and in a conspicuous location on each tract of land identified in said notice. For purposes of this Section, the notice shall be deemed posted in a "conspicuous location" if clearly visible and located in the immediate vicinity where the entrance road or trail providing vehicular access to the subject tract meets the nearest public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
844:
During the period of timber harvesting operations, the timber harvester shall comply with the following:
(1) All harvesting operations shall be conducted on the tract identified in the notice and off public roads and rights-of-way. Logging and skidding of logs on public roads and rights-of-way are strictly prohibited.
(2) Ditches constituting a part of the public drainage system or otherwise benefitting a public right-of-way shall be kept clear of all debris and residue at all times to permit proper drainage.
(3) There shall be no blockage of public roads or rights-of-way at the access site, and all public roads and rights-of-way must remain open and kept free of debris and residue at all times.
(4) No equipment, trucks, trailers, or other personal property shall be parked or located on any public road or right-of-way.
(5) Mud shall not be carried onto paved public roads by logging vehicles. Where necessary, a temporary construction exit of gravel shall be maintained by the timber harvester to eliminate any hazard to traffic or unsightly conditions on the public right-of-way.
(6) During periods of rain or inclement weather, logging vehicles shall not be operated over the unimproved public roads when such travel causes sufficient damage to the road system that the passage of smaller and lighter vehicles is hampered.

In addition to any other fees and charges authorized or implied by this chapter, the following fees and charges shall also be authorized in connection with the county water system:
(1) Delinquent billed accounts. All billed accounts are due and payable on the billing date. Billed accounts not paid within 30 days from the billing date are delinquent, and service may be disconnected by the county and a service charge added to the account. This delinquent service charge is applicable to each service call to discontinue service for delinquent accounts. The customer will be charged for the service call even if the service is not disconnected.
(2) Service calls. All customer service calls shall be charged to the customer requesting the service in accordance with a fee schedule established by the county reflecting as closely as possible the actual cost to the county for rendering the services. Restoration of service will only be made during normal working hours.
(3) Meter reinstallation due to nonpayment or failure to apply for service. A service charge to reinstall a meter shall be levied.
(4) Meter replacement, damage. The county shall determine charges to be assessed against any person causing damage to any part of the water system. Without limiting the foregoing, a charge (inclusive of the service call) will be made to replace a meter which has been damaged or frozen, or has in any way been made inoperative. The damaged meter must be returned to the county.
(5) Meter missing or stolen, replacement. A charge, based upon county cost, will be made to replace a missing or stolen meter.
(6) Miscellaneous service calls. Service calls to uncover meters, raise meters where the yard has been backfilled or landscaped, or repair meter boxes or meter connections will be billed at county cost.
(7) Returned checks. A processing fee will be charged for returned checks. If water service has been discontinued as a result of the returned check, the services in subsections (1) and (4) of this section will also apply.
(8) Failure to apply for service. A fee will be charged to users who have not properly applied for service in their own name. A separate fee shall be charged for each trip made by the county in an effort to have the customer properly and successfully apply for service. Payment must be made by the applicant for all water services utilized subsequent to the former customer discontinuing service.
(9) Water service deposits. Unless otherwise authorized in writing by the department director, a deposit is required on all accounts at the time water service is connected. This deposit shall be as defined within the rate schedule. The deposit shall be held on account for a period of not less than 24 months. After an account has established an excellent payment record for a consecutive 24-month period, the deposit shall be refunded. An excellent payment record shall mean there is no incident of delinquency, returned check, or a regular pattern of payment when past due, all as determined by the department director. The method of refund will be as a credit to the account or as a separate payment. If a deposit has been refunded and the account subsequently becomes delinquent, a deposit shall be required to be reestablished on the account, or arrangements approved by the department director made, prior to reestablishment of service. If an account is closed prior to a deposit refund, the deposit amount shall be applied to the final bill and a balance mailed to the customer as a credit refund. The county shall be under no obligation to deposit any service deposits in an interest-bearing account, and any interest earned on such monies while in the control of the county shall be the exclusive property of the county.
(10) Unauthorized connection or usage. Fees will be charged for unauthorized water system connections and also for the unauthorized use of county water system services in an amount equal to the connection fees, usage fee, and other fees and charges that would have otherwise been charged for such connection and usage if the user had been authorized to make such connection and use such water services.
(11) Other services. For any services not falling within the above definitions, the county may fix a charge on the basis of cost of labor and materials required.
(12) When service charges payable; disconnection of service for failure to pay. The payment of the sum due shall be made monthly or at such other time as indicated by the county in accordance with a statement setting forth the amount due. Payment for services billed monthly and not made within 20 days from the due date shall be subject to a surcharge of ten percent of the delinquent account; provided that such surcharge shall in no event exceed the reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the county as a result of such delinquency. The amount of such surcharge shall be established, in writing, by the department director from time to time based on such costs incurred. The failure to make any monthly payments for 60 days after the original due date shall result in water service to the premises being discontinued, with or without notice. Failure to receive notice of the amount due shall in no way relieve the customer, or owner of the property served, from making payment as provided in this section. Should any customer, including the owner of the property, receiving water service fail to pay any non-reoccurring, monthly sum due pursuant to this section, the water service shall be discontinued until such sums, with penalties as provided in this chapter, are paid in full. The remedies specified herein shall be in addition to any other remedies and penalties authorized in this chapter.
(13) Reconnection charge when water service interrupted for failure to pay service charge. Upon the failure of any customer receiving water service to make payment, the water service shall be interrupted, and in that event a reconnection charge shall be assessed and collected with all arrearage due before the water service will be restored; provided that the department director may authorize that the payment of such arrearage be made in installments, as determined by the department director to be reasonable and appropriate given the particular circumstances.
(14) Oversized meter boxes. The customer shall additionally be responsible for the cost of any meter boxes or meter vaults which exceed the standard dimensions or specifications for water meter boxes prescribed by the department director, as well as any other costs and expenses incurred by the county in connection therewith.
(Code 1987, § 13-15; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)

(a) A vehicle storage facility shall be defined as a facility which is operated solely for the purpose of storing vehicles. Generally, this service will be available to insurance companies, finance companies, banks, repossession companies, individuals, governmental agencies and other related institutions. In no way should a vehicle storage facility be construed as being an automotive salvage facility or junkyard as defined under appendix A, zoning, art. III, general provisions, section 3.16, junkyards.
(b) The following are minimum guidelines which must be adhered to in the operation of a vehicle storage facility:
(1) Such facility shall only be located in an area zoned B-2.
(2) Such facility shall be located on at least a 20,000-square foot storage site.
(3) Dismantling of vehicles, in whole or in part, is prohibited.
(4) Buying and/or selling or parts or vehicles in any manner is prohibited.
(5) Repairs to vehicles on the site, other than emergency repairs which may be required to get a vehicle cranked and removed, are prohibited.
(6) Wrecked vehicles or vehicles which are otherwise inoperable shall be removed from the site within 120 days from the initial date of storage (unless requested by a law enforcement officer to keep a vehicle at the site for a longer period).
(7) Reasonable surveillance for security purposes shall be provided by the operator of the vehicle storage facility.
(8) The facility shall be fenced with a heavy-duty wire fence not less than six feet in height with three strands of barbed wire around the top of said fence, said barbed wire to be angled outward of said fence.
(9) Fire lanes of not less than 25 feet shall be maintained.
(10) Vehicles shall not be stored in a double-decked fashion.
(Code 1987, § 11-96; Res. of 5-3-1983(1), §§ 1, 2; Res. of 6-3-1986, §§ 1, 2)

No towing and recovery service operator may be listed on any one list more than once, and may in no event use alternate legal entities or employ other strategies so as to effectively circumvent said limitation. When a towing and recovery service operator has failed or refused to respond as required herein, or has failed to reach a vehicle within the time prescribed herein, said operator shall be passed over on the applicable rotation list and shall be deemed to have responded for purposes of determining selection on the following call. The county 911 central dispatcher (or other authorized officer) shall call towing and recovery service operators in accordance with the applicable rotating list based on the instructions of the public safety officer or other responsible official at the scene.

(a) A license or an application for a license under this article may be denied, suspended or revoked only for due cause as defined in subsection (c) of this section. A license may be denied or suspended by the licensing officer as set forth in this article; provided, however, that a license may be revoked only after a hearing before the governing authority of the county upon a prior written notice to the applicant or licensee of the time, place and purpose of such hearing and a statement of the reason why the license is to be revoked. Three days' notice shall be deemed reasonable, but shorter or longer periods of notice shall be authorized as the board of commissioners may deem the circumstances justify. Unless the circumstances otherwise justify, the hearing shall be generally held no later than 45 days after the fully completed application is filed with the licensing officer, or after the licensing officer has suspended a license. If a license is denied by the licensing officer under this article, the reasons for such denial shall be set forth in writing to the applicant. The applicant shall have 30 days following receipt of notice of denial to appeal the decision of the licensing officer to the governing authority, which shall review such application de novo at the next regular meeting of the governing authority following receipt of any such appeal, or, at the election of said governing authority, at a special meeting within 45 days following said appeal; provided, however, that any appeal received within ten business days prior to the next regular meeting of the governing authority shall be heard at the second regularly scheduled meeting of said governing authority following receipt of said appeal. If the governing authority affirms the decision of the licensing officer, then the license shall be denied. If the decision of the licensing officer is reversed, then the license shall be issued to the applicant. Alternatively, the governing authority may elect to issue the license subject to such reasonable conditions as the governing authority deems appropriate.
(b) The licensing officer may suspend a license where there is evidence of due cause under subsection (c) of this section for revoking the license. Such action by the licensing officer shall be reported, in writing, to the governing authority. This action shall be reviewed at the next regular meeting of the governing authority, or, at the election of said governing authority, at a special meeting within 30 days following said suspension. If the governing authority affirms the decision of the licensing officer, then the license shall be permanently revoked. If the decision of the licensing officer is reversed, then the license shall be returned to the licensee immediately. Alternatively, the governing authority may elect to return the license to the licensee subject to such reasonable conditions as the governing authority deems appropriate.
(c) A license or application therefor under this article may be denied, suspended or revoked if one or more of the following exists:
(1) The applicant or licensee has failed to obtain any paper, permit, approval, or document required under this article.
(2) The applicant or licensee has supplied false information to the licensing officer or the governing authority.
(3) The applicant or licensee has violated any federal, state, or local statute, ordinance, regulation, rule, or law applicable to the towing and recovery services, to include, without limitation, any provision contained in this article.
(4) Allowing any condition relating to the towing and recovery services that endangers public health or safety.
(d) Unless otherwise determined by the board of commissioners following a hearing as provided herein, any licensee may petition for reinstatement of any license revoked hereunder no sooner than six months from the date of revocation. Such petition shall be submitted on forms provided by the county, and shall first be reviewed by the Liberty County 911 Board (or other person or body designated by the county administrator), who, following a hearing in the matter, shall make a recommendation regarding reinstatement to the board of commissioners. Said recommendation shall be nonbinding, and shall be decided by the board of commissioners following a subsequent hearing in matter.
(Code 1987, § 16-37; Ord. No. 2010-001, § I, 2-2-2010; Ord. No. 2010-002, § I, 4-6-2010)

918:
(a) Subdivisions of freestanding single-family homes shall have eight-inch or larger water mains with three-way fire hydrants spaced no more than 450 feet apart.
(b) Approved subdivisions of multifamily residential units, including town homes, shall have eight-inch or larger water mains installed. Three-way type fire hydrants, with a minimum of two inch and one large diameter discharge nozzles, shall be located to permit all exterior portions of all buildings to be reached with hose lays not to exceed 400 feet by road travel. Each hydrant shall be capable of providing a minimum flow of 1,000 gallons per minute (GPM) at 20 pounds per square inch (psi) residual pressure. Verification of water flow GPM shall be conducted as set forth in NFPA 291, Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants. This subsection shall not apply to a hose that lays may be extended to 500 feet for buildings with NFPA compliant automatic fire sprinkler systems.
(c) Industrial, commercial, and other nonresidential developments shall have 12-inch or larger water mains installed with three-way fire hydrants, with a minimum of two and a half inch and one large diameter discharge nozzles, spaced no more than 300 feet apart along dedicated roadways. Fire hydrants shall be placed so that all exterior portions of all buildings shall be reached with hose lays not to exceed 400 feet by road travel. Water mains of a minimum of eight inches with a minimum flow of 1,250 gallons per minute may be used for hydrants not located along dedicated roadways. Verification of water flow GPM shall be conducted as set forth in NFPA 291, Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants.
(d) Existing six-inch or larger water mains and fire hydrants may be continued in use if all of the following criteria are met: (1) The existing fire hydrant is in compliance with the specified hose lay requirements. (2) Any additional water mains and fire hydrants to be installed to meet hose lay requirements shall be supplied by a minimum of eight-inch or larger water main. (3) The existing fire hydrant shall provide a minimum of 1,000 gallons of water per minute at 20 psi residual pressure. Verification of water flow shall be in accordance with NFPA 291, Fire Flow Testing and Marking of Hydrants.
(e) Commercial, industrial, or nonresidential buildings provided with automatic fire sprinkler or standpipe systems shall have a three-way type fire hydrant placed within 150 feet of the fire department connection (FDC).
(f) Residential multifamily occupancies, residential board and care large facilities, and day care centers provided with automatic fire sprinkler protection or standpipe systems shall have a three-way fire hydrant placed within 150 feet of the fire department connection (FDC).
(Ord. No. 2026-002, § I, eff. 3-1-2026)

934:
(a) Permits and fees.
(1) Permits for open burning at or on development sites for the purpose of clearing land for new construction shall be obtained from fire plan review. Permits shall be registered with the communications center by the fire marshal's office.
(2) The applicant shall complete an application for an open burning permit issued by fire plan review. The applicant shall submit a plat or site plan showing the proposed location of the burn pit and information relating to the proximity of any occupied or unoccupied structure.
(3) The application, if approved, shall be accompanied by fees as established in the "Liberty County Land Development and Other Services Fee Schedule," as may be amended.
(4) No burning shall commence prior to an inspection of the site and the burn pit by a representative of the county fire marshal's office. Upon approval of the burn pit, the permit shall be valid for a period of 30 days. Permits may be extended for increments of 15-day periods without additional fees, with a maximum of two extensions.
(b) Fires requiring written permits.
(1) The only types of fires permitted for the purpose of land clearing are pit fires. Non-pit fires are not permitted for land clearing in the county. All pit fires shall be conducted in strict accordance with the "Air Curtain Destructor Operating Guide and Procedures" as published by the South Georgia Region of the environmental protection division.
(2) Pit fires shall comply with the following stipulations:
a. The pit shall be at least 300 feet from any occupied or habitable structure. This distance may be required to be increased by the fire marshal's office if needed;
b. Where a site cannot be excavated to the recommended depth(s) due to high water table and/or subsurface rock, the pit may be constructed above ground level, subject to the same state standards and procedures for a pit below ground level;
c. Only wood wastes consisting of trees, logs, large brush, stumps, leaves, and untreated lumber may be burned in the pit;
d. Leaves, sawdust or other densely packed wood wastes, paper (any type); chemically treated, coated or impregnated wood; or non-wood construction materials shall not be burned. The amount of dirt/soil mixture shall be kept to a minimum;
e. No more than one air curtain destructor is allowed to be operated within a ten-acre permitted site at one time. The air curtain destructor must be under the supervision of a trained operator at all times during operation. In the event there is a need for multiple burning pits there shall be a minimum of 1,000 feet between each burning pit;
f. Air curtain destructors shall pass an even, non-turbulent flow of air across the top of the pit. Air curtain destructors with an air duct or manifold that has been altered by bends, dents, holes, etc., and are incapable of providing an even and non-turbulent flow of air across the top of the pit shall not be approved for use;
g. The air curtain destructor shall be operated in a manner to prevent air, land or water pollution, safety/health hazards, or nuisances;
h. Tires or other rubber products, plastics, heavy oils or asphaltic base or impregnated materials, shall not be used to start or maintain air curtain destructor operations; and
i. No smoke emissions exceeding 40 percent opacity may be produced during operation except for a reasonable period during ignition and charging of the pit;
j. When the pit is cleared of ash, airborne particulate is to be minimized by wetting or mixing the ashes with dirt;
k. Diesel fuel or kerosene may be used to start pit fires.
(c) Types of burning allowed without a written permit.
(1) Burning of leaves, limbs, and natural vegetation that may fall on one's property.
a. The location for open burning of natural vegetation shall not be less than 50 feet from any structure, and not less than 25 feet from a property line. Provisions shall be made to prevent the fire from spreading to within 50 feet of any structure and 25 feet from a property line; provided, however, the minimum required distance from a structure shall be 25 feet when the pile size is less than three feet in diameter and less than two feet high.
b. Fires shall be limited to a size that can be easily controlled under the conditions and with the resources available on the property.
(2) Fires for the purpose of keeping warm.
a. Warming fires shall be contained within a metal barrel of 55 gallon capacity or less.
b. Untreated wood or lumber shall be the only material or substance permitted to be burned.
c. The container for the warming fire shall not be less than 50 feet from any structure.
d. No on-ground warming fires shall be permitted.
e. The outside temperature shall be 50 degrees Fahrenheit or less.
(3) Fires for the purpose of cooking food for human consumption.
a. Charcoal, wood, and gas grills and other open flame cooking devices shall not be operated on combustible balconies or within ten feet of combustible construction. Exception: One- and two-family dwellings.
b. LP gas grills and burners having an LP gas container with a water capacity greater than 2.5 pounds (one pound LP gas capacity) shall not be located on combustible balconies or within ten feet of combustible construction; provided, however, this subparagraph shall not apply to one- and two-family dwellings.
c. Open fires used for cooking food for human consumption shall not be less than 50 feet from any structure and provisions shall be made to prevent the fire from spreading to within 50 feet of any structure; provided, however, the minimum required distance from a structure shall be 25 feet when the pile size is less than three feet in diameter and less than two feet high.
d. Fires shall be limited to a size that can be easily controlled under the conditions and with the resources available on the property.
(4) Recreational fires in commercially available chimineas or outdoor fire places.
a. Chimineas or outdoor fireplaces shall be used according to their intended use, the manufacturer's recommendations, and the rules in section 42-46(c)(4).
b. Chimineas or outdoor fireplaces shall have a chimney, screen, or other approved method to arrest sparks.
c. Chimineas or outdoor fireplaces shall not be operated inside structures, on combustible surfaces or balconies, or within 25 feet of combustible construction.
d. Chimineas or outdoor fireplaces shall have a noncombustible surface underneath to safely catch sparks or dropping coals and ashes.
e. Untreated wood, lumber, manufactured fire logs, or charcoal shall be the only materials or substances permitted to be burned in chimineas or outdoor fireplaces.
(5) Bonfires; permit required; no fee.
a. No person shall kindle or maintain any bonfire or authorize any such fire to be kindled or maintained on any private or public land unless the location is no less than 50 feet from a structure with a size not to exceed four cubic feet of combustible materials and 100 feet from a structure with a size not to exceed five cubic feet of combustible materials.
b. For purposes of clarification, bonfires shall be limited to activities sponsored by civic, educational, religious or other groups for purpose of celebration, etc. An example would be a high school pep rally.
c. Bonfires shall be constantly attended by a competent person until such fire is extinguished.
d. Such person shall have a garden hose connected to a water supply, or other fire extinguishing equipment, capable of extinguishing the fire, readily available for use.
e. Access to communications to the fire department shall be maintained within 500 feet of the bonfire.
(d) Burning restrictions. The following rules govern all burning in the county, whether or not a written permit is required:
(1) The fire marshal's office with the concurrence of the fire chief may temporarily prohibit any and/or all outdoor fires when atmospheric conditions or local circumstances make such fire hazardous.
(2) No burning is permitted on Sundays or nights. Burning at construction sites for the clearing of land for new development shall not be conducted before or after daylight hours; provided, however, compliant bonfires, cooking fires, and recreational fires in chimineas and outdoor fireplaces may be burned on Sunday and at night provided all other criteria and restrictions are applied.
(3) No burning is permitted when prevailing winds are predicted to be, or are in excess of 15 miles per hour.
(4) No burning is permitted when the National Weather Service has issued a "Red Flag Warning." Burning shall be limited or prohibited as conditions warrant, when the National Weather Service has issued a "Fire Weather Watch."
(5) No burning is permitted during an air pollution episode, such as an air pollution alert/warning/emergency declared by proper authorities.
(6) No burning is permitted when there is fog, rain, or a cloud base that is diffused, or ill defined, or for at least one day following the passage of a cold front.
(7) No burning of solid waste or household garbage is allowed.
(8) No burning of any materials that emit a heavy dark smoke, such as rubber products, oils, roofing material, petroleum-based products, etc.
(9) No burning when smoke presents a health hazard to persons in the vicinity of the fire. The fire marshal's office shall be authorized to ban outdoor burning in a limited geographical area upon receipt of medical certification from a resident that the resident has a medical condition(s) adversely affected by smoke.
(10) No burning shall be conducted within 20 feet of flammable, combustible or explosive materials unless otherwise specified by the fire code.
(11) Burning of leaves, limbs, etc., that fall on a person's own property, may only be conducted during daylight hours.
(12) Prior notification shall be given to the state forestry commission before any agricultural burning is conducted. The term "agricultural" refers to land zoned RA-200 as defined by the county zoning ordinance.
(13) All fires shall be constantly attended by a competent person until extinguished.
(14) There shall be a garden hose connected to a water supply or other fire extinguishing equipment capable of extinguishing the fire readily available for use.
(e) Summary abatement. The staff of the fire marshal's office and personnel of the Liberty County Fire Rescue shall have the authority to summarily abate any condition which are in violation of any of the provisions of this section, and which may constitute an immediate threat to life and property. In no event shall a pit fire or other open burning continue after the fire marshal's office has revoked the permit.

(22) Any mobile food service establishment using solid fuel cooking appliances (wood, charcoal, etc.) with a fire box of five cubic feet or less, must provide either a 1.6-Gal Class K extinguisher or a water extinguisher, in addition to a Class 2-A 10BC ABC extinguisher.
(b) A mobile food service establishment park may be established on a privately-owned commercial property zoned C-2 or C-3 on a property no less than 30,000 square feet.
(c) Mobile food service establishments in a food truck park may share toilet facilities, parking spaces, outdoor temporary/permanent seating, trash receptacles, and other facilities as approved by the department of public health.
(d) A mobile food service establishment park site plan showing paved access and adequate off-street parking shall be submitted to the LCPC for review. The minimum number of designated parking spots required for a mobile food service establishment park shall be four per mobile food service establishment.
(e) The magistrate's court of Liberty County shall have jurisdiction over violations of food truck ordinance and all procedures for enforcement of said food truck ordinance. Complaints of violations of any provision of said food truck ordinance shall be brought before the magistrate's court on a citation issued by said code enforcement officer or the chief magistrate of Liberty County and shall be prosecuted through that court. Service of citation shall be performed by the constable of the magistrate's court of Liberty County, Georgia.
Violations of this article are subject to the following sanctions, which may not be waived or reduced, and which may be combined with any other legal remedy available to the county:
(1) First violation: $500.00.
(2) Second violation within 12 months of the first: $750.00.
(3) Third violation within 12 months of the first: $1,000.00 and revocation of the mobile food service establishment license. Mobile food service establishment license approvals will be revoked for the remainder of the calendar year.
(Ord. No. 2026-002, § I, eff. 3-1-2026)
951:
(a) Each mobile food service establishment shall provide a suitably sized receptacle for trash, which shall be located within ten feet of the service window of the unit. It shall be maintained and regularly emptied. All waste generated by the mobile food service establishment's operation, including that associated with its customers and staff, must be disposed of at the base of operation or another approved location.
(b) The area within which a mobile food service establishment operates shall, at all times, be kept clean and free from trash, garbage, rubble and debris. For purposes of this section, a mobile food service establishment shall be responsible for operating in a safe and hygienic space to conduct business.
(Ord. No. 2026-002, § I, eff. 3-1-2026)
952:
(a) Prior to the operation of any combustible gas-fueled appliances, all visible connections shall be inspected for leakage utilizing a combustible gas detector. Detected leaks shall be repaired before any gas-fueled appliance is operated.
(b) Propane and natural gas tanks shall be shut off while the mobile food vehicle is in motion, unless the tank is equipped with an impact detection shut off device approved by the U.S. DOT. Propane and natural gas tanks must always be shut off while the vehicle is unattended and/or in overnight storage. Mounted tanks must be secure (NFPA 58 5.2.4) and conform with NFPA standards relating to the safe mounting of tanks as described in NFPA 58 6.23.3.3. and be capable of withstanding impact requirements as required by the NFPA (NFPA 58 6.23.3.4.).
(c) All mobile food service establishments shall be equipped with a readily accessible multipurpose dry chemical portable fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of 2A 10BC. All mobile food service establishments utilizing fats or cooking oils, including those that produce grease, grease laden vapors or oily byproducts, shall, in addition to the ABC fire extinguisher, be equipped with a readily accessible Class K portable fire extinguisher. All required fire extinguishers shall be maintained in compliance with National Fire Protection Association 10, as amended.
(d) Propane and natural gas tanks shall be shut off while the mobile food vehicle is in motion, unless the tank is equipped with an impact detection shut off device approved by the U.S. DOT. Mobile food service establishments are prohibited from igniting, starting or operating any cooking appliances requiring heat, electricity or combustible gases while traveling upon any street, road or highway. Food warming or hot holding appliances are exempt from this requirement.
(e) Emission of exhaust gases or smoke shall not be handled in such a manner as to constitute a nuisance, pursuant to section 11.7 of the ordinance.
(f) A mobile food service establishments shall be maintained and regularly cleaned to minimize the buildup of grease and other combustible residues. This includes all interior and exterior surfaces upon which grease can or may accumulate including, but not limited to, hold filter surfaces, plenums, ducts, exhaust fans and exterior cowling.
(g) All mobile food service establishment fire suppression systems shall be inspected and maintained in accordance with the applicable provisions of the National Fire Protection Association. The system shall be tagged in accordance with the Rules and Regulations of the Georgia Safety Fire Commissioner.
(h) Liquified petroleum gas systems on mobile food vehicles and temporary cooking operations shall comply with the currently adopted IFC Section 319-.8 and Chapter 61, NFPA 5 and Chapter 120-3-6.
(i) A listed LP gas alarm shall be installed within the vehicle in the vicinity of LP gas system components, in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions per IFC Section 319.8.5.
(j) A shutoff valve shall be readily accessible and identified with a sign permanently affixed to the vehicle in reflective decal material with letters a minimum of two inches.
(k) Fabric awnings, if present, shall be fire rated to comply with IFC Section 3104 and NFPA 701. Mobile food service operators shall provide documentation or remove fabric awning.
(Ord. No. 2026-002, § I, eff. 3-1-2026)
953:

For the purposes of this article:
(1) "Consumer fireworks" means any small fireworks devices containing restricted amounts of pyrotechnic composition, designed primarily to produce visible or audible effects by combustion, that comply with the construction, chemical composition, and labeling regulations of the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission, as provided for in Parts 1500 and 1507 of Title 16 of the Code of Federal Regulations, the United States Department of Transportation, as provided for in Part 172 of Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations, and the American Pyrotechnic Association, as provided for in the 2001 American Pyrotechnics Association Standard 87-1, and additionally shall mean Roman candles.
(2) "Consumer fireworks retail sales facility" (CFRS facility). A permanent or temporary building or structure, CFRS stand, tent, canopy or membrane structure that is used primarily for the retail display and sale of consumer fireworks.
(3) "Consumer fireworks retail sales stand." A temporary or permanent building or structure that has a floor area not greater than 800 square feet, other than tent, canopies or membrane structures, that is used primarily for the retail display and sales of consumer fireworks to the public
(4) "Consumer fireworks retail sales facility" means a permanent or temporary building or structure, stand, tent, canopy or membrane structure that is used primarily for the retail display and sale of consumer fireworks to the public. Said definition shall not apply to facilities or stores where the consumer fireworks are in packages in which the total quantity of fireworks on hand does not exceed 125 pounds (net) [56.8 kilograms] of pyrotechnic composition or, in a building protected throughout with an approved automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 13, Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems, not to exceed 250 pounds (net) [113.6 kilograms] of pyrotechnic composition.
(5) "Consumer fireworks storage building." A building in which finished consumer fireworks are received, stored and shipped, but in which no manufacturing is performed. Said definition shall not apply to facilities or stores where the consumer fireworks are in packages in which the total quantity of fireworks on hand does not exceed 125 pounds (net) [56.8 kilograms] of pyrotechnic composition or, in a building protected throughout with an approved automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 13, Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems, not to exceed 250 pounds (net) [113.6 kilograms] of pyrotechnic composition.
(6) "Permanent" as applied to buildings or structures: A building or structure affixed to a foundation on a site and having fixed utility connections that is intended to remain on the site for more than 180 consecutive calendar days.
(7) "Temporary" as applied to buildings or structures: A building or structure not meeting the definition for permanent structure. As applied to electrical power and wiring: electrical service in use or in place for a period of ninety (90) consecutive calendar days or less
(8) "Fireworks" means any combustible or explosive composition or any substance or combination of substances or article prepared for the purpose of producing a visible or audible effect by combustion, explosion, deflagration, or detonation, including blank cartridges, firecrackers, torpedoes, skyrockets, bombs, sparklers, and other combustibles and explosives of like construction, as well as articles containing any explosive or flammable compound and tablets and other devices containing an explosive substance. The term "consumer fireworks" or "fireworks" shall not include:
a. Model rockets and model rocket engines, designed, sold and used for the purpose of propelling recoverable aero models; toy pistol paper caps in which the explosive content does not average more than 0.25 grains of explosive mixture per paper cap; nor toy pistols, toy cannons, toy canes, toy guns, or other devises using such paper caps; nor shall the term "consumer fireworks" or "fireworks" include ammunition consumed by weapons used for sporting and hunting purposes; and
b. Wire or wood sparklers of 100 grams or less of mixture per item; other sparkling items which are non-explosive and non-aerial and contain 75 grams or less of chemical compound per tube or a total of 500 grams or less for multiple tubes; snake and glow worms; smoke devices; or trick noise makers which include paper streamers, party poppers, string poppers, snappers, and drop pops each
(9) It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation or other entity to sell, offer to sell or use, explode, cause to be exploded, possess, manufacture, transport or store any fireworks within the corporate limits of the city, except as may be permitted under the provisions of O.C.G.A. tit. 25, Ch. 10, and the "Rules and Regulations of the Safety Fire Commissioner," Chapter 120-3-22. Consisting of 0.25 grains or less of explosive mixture.
